title: Big Food Companies Use Legal Battles to Block Health Rules
subtitle: Global health leaders say corporations are fighting government efforts to reduce obesity by taking them to court.

summary.en: The World Health Organization reports that major food companies are suing governments to stop healthy eating policies. These companies often try to block warning labels and taxes on ultra-processed foods. Although many companies claim to support public health, they frequently use legal action to delay new rules. These lawsuits have caused years of delays and cost countries billions in legal and healthcare expenses. Experts warn that this behavior makes it harder for nations to protect their citizens from diet-related diseases.
summary.zh: 世界衛生組織指出，大型食品公司正透過控告政府來阻撓健康飲食政策。這些企業常試圖阻擋超加工食品的警語標示與稅收政策。儘管許多公司宣稱支持公共衛生，卻頻繁利用法律手段拖延新規定。這些訴訟已造成長年的延宕，並讓各國在法律與醫療支出上損失數十億美元。專家警告，這種行為使得各國更難保護國民免受飲食相關疾病的威脅。

paragraphs.en: The world is currently facing a serious health challenge as obesity rates continue to rise. According to The Guardian Health, nearly one billion people around the globe are living with obesity. This condition is a major cause of heart disease, type 2 diabetes, and cancer. As a result, many governments are trying to introduce new rules to help people eat better. These rules include putting warning labels on food packaging, limiting advertisements for unhealthy snacks, and adding taxes to junk food.
paragraphs.zh: 全球目前正面臨嚴峻的健康挑戰，肥胖率持續攀升。根據《衛報健康》（The Guardian Health）報導，全球有近十億人飽受肥胖之苦。這種狀況是心臟病、第二型糖尿病與癌症的主要成因。因此，許多政府正試圖推行新規定以協助民眾改善飲食，這些措施包括在食品包裝上加註警語、限制不健康零食的廣告，以及對垃圾食物課稅。

paragraphs.en: However, these efforts are facing strong resistance from the world’s largest ultra-processed food corporations. While these companies often say in public that they want to help people make healthy choices, their actions in court tell a different story. According to The Guardian Health, an investigation found that these companies have filed 235 lawsuits between 2010 and 2025 in countries like the US, the UK, Mexico, Brazil, and Colombia. These legal actions are designed to overturn, weaken, or delay government health policies.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，這些努力正遭遇全球大型超加工食品企業的強烈抵制。儘管這些公司常在公開場合宣稱致力於協助民眾做出健康選擇，但其在法庭上的作為卻是另一回事。《衛報健康》的一項調查發現，這些企業在二零一零年至二零二五年期間，於美國、英國、墨西哥、巴西與哥倫比亞等國發起了兩百三十五起訴訟。這些法律行動旨在推翻、削弱或拖延政府的健康政策。

paragraphs.en: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the director general of the World Health Organization, has spoken out against these tactics. He noted that when companies put their profits above public health, they often try to create doubt and stop new regulations. He explained that these legal battles have created a 'regulatory chill.' This means that because of the threat of expensive lawsuits, other governments may become too afraid to pass their own health laws. This stops important changes from happening, even when those changes could save lives.
paragraphs.zh: 世界衛生組織（World Health Organization）秘書長譚德塞（Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus）公開抨擊這些手段。他指出，當企業將利潤置於公共衛生之上時，往往會試圖製造疑慮並阻撓新法規。他解釋說，這些法律攻防戰造成了「法規寒蟬效應」。這意味著由於面臨昂貴訴訟的威脅，其他政府可能會因恐懼而不敢通過自身的健康法案。即便這些變革能挽救生命，卻也因此停滯不前。

paragraphs.en: Even though the food companies lose most of these cases, the lawsuits still achieve a specific goal: delay. The Guardian Health reported that these legal fights have caused nearly 600 years of combined delays. On average, each case lasts about two and a half years. During this time, governments must spend a lot of money on legal fees instead of focusing on public health. Meanwhile, the obesity crisis continues to grow, costing countries billions of dollars in healthcare expenses.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管食品公司在多數案件中敗訴，但這些訴訟仍達成了一個特定目標：拖延。《衛報健康》報導指出，這些法律爭訟累計造成了近六百年的延宕。平均而言，每起案件耗時約兩年半。在此期間，政府必須耗費鉅額資金支付法律費用，而非專注於公共衛生。與此同時，肥胖危機持續惡化，導致各國在醫療保健支出上損失數十億美元。

paragraphs.en: The investigation was a large effort involving researchers from several universities, including the University of Sydney, the University of São Paulo, and the University of Caldas. They worked alongside the Robert and Ethel Kennedy Human Rights Centre to understand how the food industry uses the legal system to push back against change. The findings show that the impact of these lawsuits goes beyond just one country or one law. By fighting these rules, the companies are trying to discourage other nations from trying to improve the health of their citizens.
paragraphs.zh: 這項調查是一項大型研究計畫，由包括雪梨大學（University of Sydney）、聖保羅大學（University of São Paulo）與卡爾達斯大學（University of Caldas）在內的多所大學研究人員共同參與。他們與羅伯特與艾瑟爾甘迺迪人權中心（Robert and Ethel Kennedy Human Rights Centre）合作，深入了解食品產業如何利用法律體系來抵制變革。調查結果顯示，這些訴訟的影響不僅限於單一國家或單一法規。透過對抗這些規定，企業正試圖嚇阻其他國家嘗試改善國民健康。

paragraphs.en: As the debate continues, the gap between what food companies say and what they do remains a major point of concern for health officials. While the companies argue they are part of the solution, the evidence suggests that they are often the ones standing in the way. For now, governments must decide how to balance the need for better public health with the pressure from powerful corporations. The outcome of this struggle will likely shape the future of what we eat and how we protect the health of people around the world.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著辯論持續進行，食品公司言行不一的落差仍是衛生官員關注的重大議題。雖然這些公司辯稱自己是解決方案的一部分，但證據顯示，他們往往才是阻礙進步的絆腳石。目前，各國政府必須在改善公共衛生的需求與強大企業的壓力之間取得平衡。這場角力的結果，很可能會決定我們未來的飲食方式，以及我們如何保護全球民眾的健康。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To publicly express an opinion, especially in order to protest or defend something.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 公開表達意見（通常是為了抗議或捍衛某事）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 這是 speak out 的過去分詞形式，表示公開反對某事。文中：Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the director general of the World Health Organization, has spoken out against these tactics.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A discouraging or suppressing effect on an action or process.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 對某種行動或過程產生的抑制或冷卻效果。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（寒冷），這裡指對政策推動的阻礙作用。文中：He explained that these legal battles have created a 'regulatory chill.'

keyTerms.definitionEn: To resist or oppose a plan, idea, or change.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 抵抗、反對或阻撓某項計畫、想法或變革。
keyTerms.noteZh: 這裡指企業運用法律手段來阻撓政策推動。文中：They worked alongside the Robert and Ethel Kennedy Human Rights Centre to understand how the food industry uses the legal system to push back against change.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Preventing something from happening or making progress.
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面上是「站在路中間」，引申為阻礙進步。文中：While the companies argue they are part of the solution, the evidence suggests that they are often the ones standing in the way.

sources.title: Ultra-processed food companies hindering health drives by suing countries, says WHO

quiz.question: According to the investigation, what is the primary reason food companies file lawsuits against governments?

options.A: To prove that their products are healthier than the government claims.
options.B: To overturn, weaken, or delay the implementation of new health policies.
options.C: To force governments to pay for the legal fees of the corporations.
options.D: To change the warning labels on their packaging to be more informative.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，文中明確指出這些法律行動的目的是「overturn, weaken, or delay government health policies」（推翻、削弱或延遲政府的健康政策）。選項 A 並非法律訴訟的目的；選項 C 雖然提到法律費用，但那是政府因訴訟而承擔的負擔，而非企業提告的動機；選項 D 與文意相反，企業提告是為了阻止這些標籤出現，而非為了讓標籤更具資訊性。

quiz.question: What is the most likely consequence of a 'regulatory chill' as described in the text?

options.A: Food companies will start to lower the prices of their products.
options.B: Governments will spend more money on public health initiatives.
options.C: Other governments may hesitate to pass health laws to avoid legal battles.
options.D: The number of lawsuits filed by food companies will decrease significantly.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第三段，Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus 解釋「regulatory chill」是指政府因為害怕昂貴的訴訟而不敢推行健康法規。這暗示了其他國家會因為看到前例而採取觀望或退縮的態度。選項 A 與文中提到的企業行為不符；選項 B 與文中提到的政府被迫將錢花在法律費用上相矛盾；選項 D 則缺乏依據，文中並未暗示訴訟數量會因寒蟬效應而減少。

quiz.question: In the third paragraph, what does the phrase 'regulatory chill' imply about the atmosphere created by food corporations?

options.A: A state of fear that prevents governments from taking action.
options.B: A period of cold weather that affects food production.
options.C: A relaxed approach to monitoring food safety standards.
options.D: A successful collaboration between companies and regulators.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。文中提到「regulatory chill」是因為企業威脅要提告，導致政府「too afraid to pass their own health laws」（太害怕而不敢通過自己的健康法），因此這是一種因恐懼而導致政策停滯的狀態。選項 B 是對「chill」的字面誤解；選項 C 與文意完全相反，因為政策是被阻止而非放鬆監管；選項 D 錯誤解讀了企業與政府之間對立的關係。

quiz.question: What is the central message of this article regarding the relationship between food corporations and public health?

options.A: Food corporations are successfully helping governments solve the obesity crisis.
options.B: Legal systems are the best way to resolve conflicts between corporations and health officials.
options.C: The obesity crisis is primarily caused by a lack of awareness about food labels.
options.D: Food corporations often prioritize profits over public health by obstructing government regulations.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。文章整體旨在探討食品巨頭如何利用法律手段阻礙政府推行改善公共健康的政策，以保護其商業利益，這與文章開頭提到的肥胖危機形成強烈對比。選項 A 與文章結論「they are often the ones standing in the way」矛盾；選項 B 錯誤，文章強調法律系統被企業濫用來拖延政策；選項 C 雖提到標籤，但並非文章的核心論點，文章重點在於企業對法規的阻撓。
